current_inference.orientation: Direct manipulation evidence outside Asteraceae supports multiple mechanisms (effective pollination plus abiotic protection) reaching seed/fruit fitness; effect transport to Cirsium remains a hypothesis.
current_inference.stickiness: A universal sticky-is-defence rule is not retained. Direct floral evidence includes strong benefit in Bejaria while Cirsium has a null direct neutralization result elsewhere in the repository; whole-plant Datura also shows substantial demographic costs. Context-dependent defence is the working hypothesis.
current_inference.display: Direct manipulation supports simultaneous pollinator-attraction benefit and seed-predator cost, but broad-angiosperm numerical common-effect extraction is incomplete.

next_meta_actions: extract raw/group summaries for Ipomopsis display manipulation
extract comparable quantitative endpoints for Aquilegia glandular-trichome manipulation
add additional independent orientation manipulations with seed/fruit endpoints
do not pool different response metrics until an explicit common estimand or multivariate model is preregistered
claim_boundary: Candidate calibration/effect-extraction registry only; no pooled across-angiosperm effect and no Cirsium adaptation claim.
